---
title: "SQL Workshop"
---

This workshop introduces you to SQL, a powerful language originally designed for managing and querying relational databases and now widely used across data applications. You’ll learn what a relational database is and master the basics of SQL syntax for retrieving data with queries. Taking a hands-on approach, the workshop gives you plenty of opportunities to practise writing and running SQL queries through practical exercises.

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### What To Prepare

In this workshop, we will mostly use [Google Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/) as our coding environment. Google Colab is a hosted Jupyter Notebook service that requires no setup to use and provides free access to computing resources.

Please make sure you have a Google account and can access Google Colab. If you have not used Google Colab before, please go through the three Colab tutorials below to get familiar with the environment.

-   [Welcome to Colab!](https://colab.research.google.com/notebooks/intro.ipynb)
-   [Overview of Colab](https://colab.research.google.com/notebooks/basic_features_overview.ipynb)
-   [Guide to Markdown](https://colab.research.google.com/notebooks/markdown_guide.ipynb)

If you want to get a head start on SQL before the workshop, you can work through the following online course. (It is not required, but it will help you get more out of the workshop.)

-   [Learning SQL Programming by Scott Simpson](https://www.linkedin.com/learning/learning-sql-programming-8382385){target="_blank"} (1h 27m).

This online course is available through LinkedIn Learning. You can get free access to LinkedIn Learning by applying for a Toronto Public Library (TPL) card, and login LinkedIn Learning via its [TPL get-started page](https://www.linkedin.com/learning-login/go/tpl){target="_blank"}. (You can get a TPL [Digital Access Card](https://tpl.ca/help/your-library-card/){target="_blank"} without even visiting a library branch.)
